lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The Atomic Bachelor Pad, one fifteen point six. A high fidelity demonstration. Please sit in the exact centre of the sofa.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: You're listening to the Atomic Bachelor Pad, in stereo. If you can only hear half of this sentence, you are sitting too far to the left.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The Atomic Bachelor Pad. Two speakers. One sofa. Unlimited sophistication.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The Atomic Bachelor Pad. The lamps are low, the dials are glowing, and the bongos are in position. Your left. Always your left.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Good morning from the Atomic Bachelor Pad. Monty Stereo, in a dressing gown, between two very large speakers.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Now hear the bongos travel... to your left speaker.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: There. Did you feel that? That, my friends, is the future. Some men go to the moon. I sit very still, and let the bongos come to me.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Let's take a moment with that vibraphone. Notice the bouquet. A bright attack, a long, warm finish, and notes of chrome and walnut.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Nineteen sixty two was an exceptional year for the vibraphone. Best served slightly chilled, from the right speaker.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Since nineteen sixty one, the orchestra on this next one has been playing table tennis across my living room. Trumpet, left. Trombone, right. Trumpet, left.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The score stands at four thousand two hundred and six all. Nobody has ever won. Nobody wants to.

clips.title: The Theremin Is in the Hallway

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Some of you have written in to ask where the theremin is. It is not in the left speaker. It is not in the right speaker.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: In my professional opinion, the theremin is in the hallway. It has been there since Tuesday. I've left it a sandwich.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: A word to listeners with only one speaker. I'm sorry. Truly.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Please tilt your head slightly to one side, and imagine the other half. Many fine people get by this way. They are very brave.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: A word for the operator on the relay ship. I understand your console has a great many speakers. Little ones, all over the cabin.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: I'd love to come aboard with a tape measure and find you the sweet spot. Everybody deserves a sweet spot. Even in deep space. Especially there.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: This demonstration is brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders, for mounting your loudspeakers at the correct height. Which is ear height, plus a little, for drama.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. Up and slightly to the left is a lifestyle.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The neighbours at Lot Eleven have asked me to turn it down. I've explained to them that it isn't loud. It's wide.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: They've asked me to make it narrower. I'm considering it. In the meantime, here is something very, very wide.

clips.title: Review: The Quiet Corner with Greg

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Last night The Quiet Corner with Greg aired on the Lounge at the End of Time. I listened on the Model Twelve, with everything turned all the way up.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Greg was located dead centre, at a level of almost nothing. On a lesser console, you'd hear silence. On mine, you could hear him being shy. Four stars.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Friends, is your living room only half alive? A message from Starburst Hi-Fi of Futureville.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Introducing the Futureville Fidelity Console, Model Twelve. Eleven feet of solid walnut, forty two glowing valves, and a turntable so smooth the music never knows it's moving.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Now with the Twin Cathedral loudspeakers. So large and so faithful that your trombone section will need a room of its own. We'll build it for you. Extension included.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Hear a pin drop. Hear which side of the room it dropped on. Hear the pin's opinion of the carpet.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Starburst Hi-Fi, on the Atomic Parkway. Hear everything. Twice. In stereo.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen, this is a stereo test. Please put down your drink, find the chalk mark on the carpet, and sit on it.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: This is the left speaker. Hello.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: This is the right speaker. Hello.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: If those both came from the same place, please call a professional.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: You will now hear a single bongo, placed precisely in the centre. If it seems to come from your kitchen, then there is a bongo in your kitchen. Please deal with that separately.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Next, a test of depth. Here is a cymbal, very far away. Further. Further still.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: That cymbal is now in the next county. Your speakers are working beautifully.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Finally, a test of silence. Please listen carefully.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: That was high fidelity silence, in stereo. Some of you heard the left half. Well done.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: That concludes the stereo test. You may relax. Not too much. Mind your posture.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to Morning Calibration, on the Atomic Bachelor Pad. Before coffee, before the newspaper, before anything at all, we tune the room.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Over breakfast, I've moved the left speaker two inches towards the window. The grapefruit sounds noticeably brighter.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: People think high fidelity is about music. It's about everything. The toast has never been so well defined.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to Stereo at Six, on the Atomic Bachelor Pad. The martinis are cold, the valves are warm, and the speakers are exactly the right distance apart.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Tonight's pairing. A slow bossa nova, with a dry martini and a good armchair.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The martini sits in the centre. The guitar sits on the left. And you sit exactly where I tell you to sit.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: This is the Sunken Lounge, on the Atomic Bachelor Pad. Step down three carpeted steps, into the very best seat in Futureville. Mind the rug.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Late in the sunken lounge. The starburst clock says ten past eleven, and the rocket on the horizon is lit up for the night.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: This is the hour for strings. Strings are at their best after ten, once they've had a chance to breathe.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: A special Halloween demonstration. Hear the haunted theremin travel from your left speaker, to your right speaker, and then out of the room entirely, and up the stairs.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: I don't have any stairs. It's a split level. Nevertheless. Footsteps.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Listeners report a missing moon. I've checked both speakers. It is not in the left. It is not in the right.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: If it's anywhere, it's in the centre image, which is where I keep everything I can't explain.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Smell is not a stereo phenomenon. And yet, this evening, the toast is distinctly to the left.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Lovely separation. Somebody has a very good kitchen.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Everybody is humming the same song, and nobody can finish it. I can tell you this much.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: It starts in the left speaker, crosses the room, and never quite arrives on the right.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Three knocks at the front door. Left, centre, right. A perfect stereo knock.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: There was nobody there. I'd like to buy the knock anyway.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: The sky over Futureville has gone a colour nobody has a word for.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: I couldn't tell you what it is. I can tell you it would look terrific on a speaker cabinet.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: A pigeon has walked into the living room, and is standing on the chalk mark, exactly between the speakers.

lines.speaker: Monty Stereo
lines.text: Found the sweet spot first time. That bird has been in this business longer than I have.
